summary: Stable releases publish only when the Compounding Manager acts after the Fractal Product Lead records GO for the exact full candidate source SHA. Daily candidates target that SHA without creating a tag; publication creates the tag and preserves the optional operator summary verbatim.

rules.detail: No runtime checkpoint or retention changes. Daily release cleanup deletes older semantic-version unpublished drafts only after a newer complete candidate is successfully created; published releases and prereleases are untouched.

compatibility.detail: No binary or wire changes; consumers must pin only published release tags, never draft candidate version names.

downtime.detail: No runtime deployment occurs when creating a candidate.

manual.detail: Candidate creation accepts an optional summary input (default empty) that publication preserves verbatim. After the Fractal Product Lead records GO for the full candidate SHA, the Compounding Manager dispatches release-daily.yml on main with mode=publish, tag, sha and go_ref. Publication refuses a candidate when a newer semantic-version draft exists unless the optional allow_superseded input (default empty) exactly names the selected older tag. Candidate creation alone creates no tag, publishes nothing and never advances compatibility baselines. See docs/st3/binary-releases.md for the exact command and optional override.

recovery.detail: A rejected publish leaves the candidate unpublished. Correct the SHA or GO reference, select the newer candidate, or deliberately set allow_superseded to the selected older tag before dispatching again. Failed candidate creation does not delete older drafts. Never move an existing candidate or published tag.
